the dimensions of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> are the same

solution.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>A</mi><mtext>sin</mtext><mo>⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><mtext>cos</mtext><mo>⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>; Dimensions of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> would be same as two quantities can be added only when they have same dimensions. So from given equation, we can say that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi></math> is dimensionless.
